page: Amazon Web Services c8i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores on the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, placing the instance in the top 10% for multi-core CPU stress tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. The Intel Xeon processors support advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which drive top-tier performance in extended instruction tests, cryptography, and database operations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% for both cached and uncached read operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, falling into the middle 50% in single-core stress tests.

The instance is highly optimized for parallel processing workloads, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and large-scale database operations, as evidenced by its top-tier Redis SET throughput and static web serving capabilities. It also demonstrates strong capabilities for LLM inference prompt processing and text generation. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. This hardware profile offers high compute density and memory bandwidth efficiency for enterprise-scale parallel computing, high-performance web serving, and intensive simulation workloads.
